metadata.value: denoising and classification in the low-data regime
metadata.normalized_value: denoising and classification in the low-data regime
metadata.evidence:
We evaluate our pre-trained sparse autoencoders on the downstream tasks of denoising (for MNIST and our custom 
ImageNet patches dataset) and classification in the low-data regime (for MNIST only).
metadata.reason: Defines the downstream evaluation tasks and their dataset coverage.

metadata.value: The denoising performance on the test set can be measured at the end of training by providing a list with levels of random noise (measured by std of Gaussian noise; the noise is added to the input images) in the noise argument in main.py. Alternatively, eval_denoising.py can be used given a pre-trained autoencoder.

metadata.evidence:
The denoising perfomance on the test set can be measured at the end of training by providing a list with levels of 
random noise (measured by std of Gaussian noise; the noise is added to the input images) in the ```noise``` argument 
in ```main.py```.

Alternatively, ```eval_denoising.py``` can be used given a pre-trained autoencoder.
metadata.reason: Provides the denoising evaluation procedure, noise parameter, and evaluation script.

metadata.value: compute_codes.py creates a dataset containing the codes for each MNIST image; eval_classification.py measures classification performance with a set number of training samples per class.
metadata.normalized_value: compute_codes.py creates a dataset containing the codes for each MNIST image; eval_classification.py measures classification performance with a set number of training samples per class.
metadata.evidence:
Step 1: Given a pre-trained encoder, ```compute_codes.py``` can be used to create a dataset containing the codes 
for each MNIST image.

Step 2: Using the dataset from the previous step, ```eval_classification.py``` can be used to measure classification 
performance with a set number of training samples per class.
metadata.reason: Specifies the reproducible two-step workflow for evaluating code separability.
